the direct hydrogenation of carbon dioxide over hybrid catalysts with copper oxide and zirconia as a metal function and heteropoly acids as a Bronsted acid function is a promising process for the synthesis of dimethyl ether.
the CuO/ZrnO2-Montmorillonite K-10 modified with heteropolyacids is a very promising catalytic system for the direct synthesis of DME from CO2 and H, mixture.
the direct hydrogenation of a CO2 and a H2 mixture over hybrid catalysts is possible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of catalysts for DME synthesis, which are hybrid catalysts.
the direct synthesis of DME from the mixture CO, and H2 over hybrid catalysts.
the development and optimization of the synthesis of hybrid catalyst for direct hydrogenation of carbon dioxide to dimethyl ether.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hybrid catalysts obtained by impregnation method are characterized by higher total activity and selectivity to DME than the catalysts obtained by incipient wetness method.
hybrid CuO/Zr/H3PW12O40 catalysts prepared via impregnation method, which was characterized by the highest thermal stability and acidity, exhibited the best catalytic activity and DME selectivity.
the most active hybrid catalyst is obtained by using the impregnation method for obtaining the CuO/ZnO2 metallic function and HPA H2PW12O40 as an acidic function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best catalyst was obtained by co-precipitation of copper and zirconium salts.
the hybrid catalysts containing montmorillonite modified by heteropolyacid as acidic function and CuO/Zr02 as metallic function are very promising for DME synthesis.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the direct hydrogenation of carbon dioxide can be performed over a hybrid catalyst containing copper oxide as a metallic function, and heteropolyacides as an acidic function in the presence of montmorillonite.
the CuO/ZnO2 catalyst modified by HPA K10 is a promising catalyst for the direct hydrogenation of carbon dioxide to dimethyl ether.

the hybrid catalysts based on CuO/Zr02 as a metallic function, modified by heteropolyacid as an acidic function are promising materials for the direct hydrogenation of carbon dioxide to dimethyl ether.
